properties.displayName: Parser for Exchange events
properties.query:
// One row per email Filewall processed.
// ThreatVerdict separates what a Filewall engine found from what policy did, so severity follows
// the verdict and not the block alone:
//   Malicious        - an antivirus engine found malware (High)
//   Suspicious       - static analysis flagged the file, or its content does not match its type (Medium)
//   ProcessingFailed / NotSanitized - the file was not processed or not sanitized (Low)
//   Unsanitizable    - CDR could not rebuild the file, so it was blocked (Low)
//   PolicyBlocked    - blocked by a file type, size or encryption rule, not a malware verdict (Informational)
//   Sanitized        - CDR rebuilt the file and it was delivered (Informational)
// A message takes the most severe verdict of its attachments. EmailAttachments carries each
// attachment with its own verdict and severity; FilewallM365EmailAttachmentEvent expands it.
// FilewallMessageId is Filewall's id for the message: the Graph item id for mailbox mail, and
// "<Message-ID>@@<recipient>" for relay mail. It is not the Exchange Online NetworkMessageId.
FilewallExchange_CL
| extend IngestionTime = ingestion_time()
| extend
        direction = column_ifexists('direction', ''),
        source_folder = column_ifexists('source_folder', ''),
        internet_message_id = column_ifexists('internet_message_id', ''),
        report_url = column_ifexists('report_url', '')
| mv-apply Attachment = attachments on (
    extend AttachmentStatus = tolower(tostring(Attachment.status)), AttachmentReason = tolower(tostring(Attachment.block_reason))
    | extend Verdict = case(
        AttachmentReason == "antivirus", "Malicious",
        AttachmentReason in ("static_analysis", "type_validation"), "Suspicious",
        AttachmentReason == "cdr_init_failed" or AttachmentStatus == "failed", "ProcessingFailed",
        AttachmentStatus in ("not_supported", "not_sanitized"), "NotSanitized",
        AttachmentReason == "cdr", "Unsanitizable",
        AttachmentReason in ("file_policy", "size_limitation", "encryption_filter"), "PolicyBlocked",
        AttachmentStatus == "blocked", "Blocked",
        AttachmentStatus in ("succeed", "sanitized"), "Sanitized",
        "Unknown")
    | extend VerdictRank = case(Verdict == "Malicious", 8, Verdict == "Suspicious", 7, Verdict == "ProcessingFailed", 6, Verdict == "NotSanitized", 5, Verdict == "Unsanitizable", 4, Verdict == "Blocked", 3, Verdict == "PolicyBlocked", 2, Verdict == "Sanitized", 1, 0)
    | extend VerdictSeverity = case(VerdictRank == 8, "High", VerdictRank == 7, "Medium", VerdictRank >= 3, "Low", "Informational")
    | summarize arg_max(VerdictRank, Verdict, VerdictSeverity), EmailAttachments = make_list(bag_merge(Attachment, bag_pack("verdict", Verdict, "severity", VerdictSeverity)))
  )
| extend
        EventStartTime = TimeGenerated,
        EventEndTime = TimeGenerated,
        EventOriginalType = tostring(event_type),
        ThreatVerdict = coalesce(Verdict, "Unknown"),
        EventSeverity = coalesce(VerdictSeverity, "Informational")
| extend
        EventType = iff(ThreatVerdict in ("Malicious", "Suspicious"), "ThreatInfo", "Informational"),
        EventResult = case(status =~ "blocked", "Blocked", status =~ "partial_blocked", "Partial", status =~ "failed", "Failure", status in~ ("succeed", "sanitized"), "Success", "NA"),
        EventOriginalResultDetails = coalesce(state, summary),
        EventVendor = "ODI-X",
        EventProduct = "Filewall for Microsoft 365",
        EventUid = tostring(event_id),
        EmailSubject = subject,
        EmailSenderFrom = sender,
        EmailRecipientTo = recipient,
        EmailDirection = case(direction =~ "incoming", "Inbound", direction =~ "outgoing", "Outbound", ""),
        EmailInternetMessageId = internet_message_id,
        FilewallMessageId = mail_id,
        EventReportUrl = report_url,
        AlertPolicyId = policy_id,
        AlertPolicyName = policy_name,
        User = recipient,
        ActorUsername = sender,
        Dvc = application,
        DvcHostname = application,
        EventSchema = "Alert",
        EventSchemaVersion = "0.1.0",
        EventCount = int(1),
        timestamp = todatetime(timestamp),
        release_timestamp = todatetime(release_timestamp),
        release_by_admin = tobool(release_by_admin)
| project TimeGenerated, IngestionTime, EventStartTime, EventEndTime, EventUid, EventType, EventOriginalType, EventResult, EventOriginalResultDetails, EventSeverity, ThreatVerdict, EventVendor, EventProduct, EventSchema, EventSchemaVersion, EventCount, Dvc, DvcHostname, User, ActorUsername, EmailSubject, EmailSenderFrom, EmailRecipientTo, EmailDirection, EmailInternetMessageId, FilewallMessageId, EventReportUrl, AlertPolicyId, AlertPolicyName, application, event_id, timestamp, status, state, summary, attachments, EmailAttachments, direction, source_folder, release_timestamp, release_by_admin, release_reason

        FileStatus == "blocked", "Blocked",

        EventStartTime = TimeGenerated,

        EventOriginalType = tostring(event_type),
        EventType = case(status =~ "blocked", "FileBlocked", status =~ "succeed", "FileModified", status =~ "failed", "FileError", "FileEvent"),

        OriginalFileSha256 = tolower(original_sha256),

        SanitizedFileSha256 = tolower(new_sha256),
        SanitizedFileSha1 = tolower(new_sha1),
        EventReportUrl = report_url,
        ActorUsername = owner,
        ActorUserType = "Regular",
        User = owner,
        DvcHostname = coalesce(site_name, drive_name),
        Dvc = coalesce(site_name, drive_name),
        EventSchema = "FileEvent",
        EventSchemaVersion = "0.2.2",
        EventCount = int(1)

properties.displayName: Parser for Exchange email attachment events
properties.query:
// One row per email attachment Filewall processed, with its message's columns and its own
// ThreatVerdict and EventSeverity (see FilewallM365ExchangeEvent for the verdicts).
// The original and sanitized hashes are kept apart: OriginalFile* is the file the sender sent,
// the one to look for elsewhere; SanitizedFile* is the copy Filewall delivered in its place,
// empty when nothing was delivered.
FilewallM365ExchangeEvent()

properties.description: BlockedEmails_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.2.2

Identifies attachments in inbound email that Filewall for Microsoft 365 blocked because an antivirus engine found malware (High severity), or because static analysis flagged the file or its content does not match its file type (Medium severity).
Attachments blocked only by a policy rule (file type, size or encryption) and attachments sanitized by CDR are not malware verdicts and do not raise this alert; they stay available in the FilewallM365EmailAttachmentEvent parser.
The alert maps the recipient, the message and the original file hashes, so Microsoft Defender XDR can correlate it with other evidence for the same file or user, and it links to the message in the Filewall console.

// TimeGenerated is the email's received time, which can be well before Filewall finished with it,

| where ThreatVerdict in ("Malicious", "Suspicious")
| where EmailDirection != "Outbound"
| extend RecipientAccountName = tostring(split(EmailRecipientTo, "@")[0]), RecipientUPNSuffix = tostring(split(EmailRecipientTo, "@")[1])

properties.description: BlockedFileSeenOnDevice_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.2.2

Correlates files that Filewall for Microsoft 365 blocked as malicious or suspicious, in email attachments or in SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams, with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint file events.
A match means the original file reached a device by another path after Filewall blocked it, for example a direct download, a removable drive, another mail flow or a copy released from quarantine.
The match is on the original file hash Filewall recorded; the sanitized hash is kept in the custom details. Requires the Microsoft Defender XDR connector to stream DeviceFileEvents into the workspace.
properties.displayName: Filewall - File Filewall blocked as malicious or suspicious seen on a device
properties.query:
// Files Filewall blocked as malicious or suspicious in the last 14 days, keyed by original hash,
// matched with device file events ingested in the last hour that happened after the block.
let deviceLookback = 1h;
let FilewallBlocked = union
    (FilewallM365EmailAttachmentEvent()
    | where ThreatVerdict in ("Malicious", "Suspicious") and isnotempty(OriginalFileSha256)
    | project FilewallTime = TimeGenerated, SHA256 = OriginalFileSha256, SanitizedSHA256 = SanitizedFileSha256, ThreatVerdict, EventSeverity, FilewallFileName = AttachmentName, FilewallUser = EmailRecipientTo, FilewallSource = "exchange", BlockReason = AttachmentBlockReason, EventReportUrl),
    (FilewallM365FileEvent()
    | where ThreatVerdict in ("Malicious", "Suspicious") and isnotempty(OriginalFileSha256)
    | project FilewallTime = TimeGenerated, SHA256 = OriginalFileSha256, SanitizedSHA256 = SanitizedFileSha256, ThreatVerdict, EventSeverity, FilewallFileName = TargetFileName, FilewallUser = ActorUsername, FilewallSource = TargetFilePathType, BlockReason = block_reason, EventReportUrl)
  | summarize arg_min(FilewallTime, *) by SHA256;
DeviceFileEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(deviceLookback + 1h)
| where ingestion_time() > ago(deviceLookback)
| where isnotempty(SHA256)
| extend SHA256 = tolower(SHA256)
| join kind=inner FilewallBlocked on SHA256
| where TimeGenerated > FilewallTime
| summarize arg_min(TimeGenerated, *) by SHA256, DeviceId
| extend DeviceAccountUpn = tostring(InitiatingProcessAccountUpn)
| extend
    DeviceAccountName = iff(isnotempty(DeviceAccountUpn), tostring(split(DeviceAccountUpn, "@")[0]), InitiatingProcessAccountName),
    DeviceAccountUPNSuffix = iff(isnotempty(DeviceAccountUpn), tostring(split(DeviceAccountUpn, "@")[1]), ""),
    DeviceAccountNTDomain = iff(isempty(DeviceAccountUpn), InitiatingProcessAccountDomain, ""),
    FilewallAccountName = tostring(split(FilewallUser, "@")[0]),
    FilewallUPNSuffix = tostring(split(FilewallUser, "@")[1]),
    FileDirectory = iff(FolderPath endswith FileName, substring(FolderPath, 0, strlen(FolderPath) - strlen(FileName) - 1), FolderPath),
    Sha256Algorithm = "SHA256"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceId, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FileDirectory, FolderPath, SHA256, Sha256Algorithm, SanitizedSHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, DeviceAccountName, DeviceAccountUPNSuffix, DeviceAccountNTDomain, ThreatVerdict, EventSeverity, BlockReason, FilewallTime, FilewallFileName, FilewallUser, FilewallAccountName, FilewallUPNSuffix, FilewallSource, EventReportUrl

properties.query:
let lookback = 14d;
// only files whose content Filewall changed: the original and the sanitized hash differ
let FilewallSanitized = union
    (FilewallM365EmailAttachmentEvent()
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where ThreatVerdict == "Sanitized" and EmailDirection != "Outbound"
    | where isnotempty(OriginalFileSha256) and isnotempty(SanitizedFileSha256) and OriginalFileSha256 != SanitizedFileSha256
    | project FilewallTime = TimeGenerated, SHA256 = OriginalFileSha256, SanitizedSHA256 = SanitizedFileSha256, FilewallFileName = AttachmentName, FilewallUser = EmailRecipientTo, FilewallSource = "exchange", Sender = EmailSenderFrom, EventReportUrl),
    (FilewallM365FileEvent()
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where ThreatVerdict == "Sanitized"
    | where isnotempty(OriginalFileSha256) and isnotempty(SanitizedFileSha256) and OriginalFileSha256 != SanitizedFileSha256
    | project FilewallTime = TimeGenerated, SHA256 = OriginalFileSha256, SanitizedSHA256 = SanitizedFileSha256, FilewallFileName = TargetFileName, FilewallUser = ActorUsername, FilewallSource = TargetFilePathType, Sender = "", EventReportUrl)
  | summarize arg_min(FilewallTime, *) by SHA256;
DeviceFileEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where isnotempty(SHA256)
| extend SHA256 = tolower(SHA256)
| join kind=inner FilewallSanitized on SHA256
| where TimeGenerated > FilewallTime
| summarize FirstSeenOnDevice = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeenOnDevice = max(TimeGenerated), DeviceActions = make_set(ActionType), arg_min(TimeGenerated, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, FilewallTime, FilewallFileName, FilewallUser, FilewallSource, Sender, SanitizedSHA256, EventReportUrl) by SHA256, DeviceId
| extend
    DeviceAccountName = tostring(split(InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, "@")[0]),
    DeviceAccountUPNSuffix = tostring(split(InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, "@")[1]),
    FileDirectory = iff(FolderPath endswith FileName, substring(FolderPath, 0, strlen(FolderPath) - strlen(FileName) - 1), FolderPath),
    Sha256Algorithm = "SHA256"
| project FirstSeenOnDevice, LastSeenOnDevice, DeviceId, DeviceName, DeviceActions, FileName, FileDirectory, SHA256, Sha256Algorithm, SanitizedSHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, DeviceAccountName, DeviceAccountUPNSuffix, FilewallTime, FilewallFileName, FilewallUser, FilewallSource, Sender, EventReportUrl
| order by FirstSeenOnDevice desc

tags.name: description
tags.value:
Finds devices holding the original, unsanitized copy of a file that Filewall for Microsoft 365 sanitized, in inbound email or in SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams.
Filewall removed active content from these files before delivering them, so a device with the original hash got the file another way: a direct download, a removable drive, another mail flow or a copy released from Filewall.
Sanitizing is a policy action, not a malware verdict, so this is a hunting query rather than an alert. The sanitized hash is shown next to the original, and the report link opens the item in the Filewall console. Requires the Microsoft Defender XDR connector to stream DeviceFileEvents into the workspace.

Filewall for Microsoft 365 solution installs a Codeless (CCF/CLv2) connector that ingests Filewall activity logs for Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams into custom tables. It also installs parsers, a workbook, analytics rules that alert on malicious and suspicious files by verdict, and rules and hunting queries that correlate Filewall file hashes with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint device file events.
